target: Hillshade relief diagram for the Intelligence Brief terrain card — render a colored shaded-relief PNG from the DEM the terrain pipeline already loads, return it as a base64 data URI in the terrain section, display it in TerrainCard.
findings_summary: DEM is already in memory: services/terrain_analysis.py:_run_terrain_chain reads dem.tif into dem_arr (float64, NaN at nodata) at line 895; no second fetch needed. Viz deps already in requirements (numpy, matplotlib==3.10.5, pillow==11.3.0) — use matplotlib.colors.LightSource.shade(dem, colormaps['terrain'], blend_mode='soft', vert_exag) for a colored relief directly from the array (no extra whitebox call, no figure/Agg backend). NaN -> transparent alpha; downsample to <=256px; PNG via PIL -> base64 data URI; cap b64 length. Output flows via the existing dict -> _build_terrain_detail filters by TerrainAnalysisDetail.model_fields, so add hillshade_png_b64 to BOTH the real model (terrain_analysis.py:97) and the rasterio-missing stub (intelligence_brief.py:904) and it passes through to the streamed satellite.terrain DataField.value. NO DB, NO migration, NO new external fetch, NO spatial join — pure in-memory raster->PNG transform. Failure-safety is the key contract: the whole render is wrapped try/except -> returns None on any failure so the terrain metrics are NEVER affected. Tests: conftest_mocks mocks numpy/rasterio/whitebox only when absent, so real-render tests are skipif-gated on real numpy+matplotlib+PIL; the None-safety contract (None/junk input -> None, no raise) is always tested. GO.
